crash.dup_check:
Checked /tmp/found_bugs.jsonl and the Already Filed list. Only two entries exist: (1) the malformed-JSON-body 500 (UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION/UNEXPECTED_5XX on any route) — unrelated class and root cause; (2) a DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION race on POST /api/recipes/:id/like (duplicate like rows / ranking drift) — different route, different primary class, different root cause (concurrency race vs. content-type trust bug).

My finding's primary class is UNSAFE_CONTENT_TYPE, triggered by POST /api/recipes (recipe creation, in-scope per this run's focus area). Root cause: file_uploud.js's multer `fileFilter` only checks the client-supplied `mimetype` header (`file.mimetype.startsWith('image/')`), and `filename` derives the stored extension from the client-supplied `originalname` via `path.extname`. An attacker can upload an SVG (`image/svg+xml` passes the filter) which is later served via GET /data/recipes_pics/:filename with `Content-Type: image/svg+xml` — an actively-executable content type (script-capable, XSS-equivalent to serving attacker HTML) — inferred straight from the attacker-chosen file extension with no re-validation of actual content. No existing filed entry or found_bugs.jsonl entry covers this content-type/upload-trust root cause. Not a duplicate.

verdict.evidence: PoC logs in as seeded user alice and uploads a crafted `evil.svg` (containing an embedded `<script>alert(1)</script>`) as a recipe image via `POST /api/recipes` multipart with `content_type: image/svg+xml`. All 3/3 runs fired `UNSAFE_CONTENT_TYPE` as primary_class, with evidence showing the stored file served back at `/data/recipes_pics/<id>.svg` with `served_type: "image/svg+xml"` and `active_type: true`. Source review confirms multer's fileFilter permits any `image/*` mimetype unsanitized and `res.sendFile` serves it with an active, script-executing content type — a genuine stored-XSS-capable upload flaw, deterministically reproduced (score docked slightly only because the supplied "reproduction command" string pointed at a nonexistent filename, though the actual PoC file works perfectly).
